summary.en-US: Vim keys for Thunderbird and Betterbird that teach themselves: move, archive and reply from the keyboard, a command line with completion, and a popup that shows what every key does.

description.en-US:
Desert the mouse. The keys teach themselves.

DesertBird puts Vim keys in Thunderbird and Betterbird. It works in the mail tab, the message pane, message windows and the compose window. Press j and k to move through the thread list, a to archive, r to reply, and f to put a short label on each link and button in a message. Type the label to click it. Press : to run any command by name, with completion.

If you know Vim, most keys feel familiar. If you do not, five keys are enough on the first day: j, k, a, : and ,h for help.

You do not memorize the keys
- A which-key popup lists the keys that can follow and what each does. It opens after a short pause on a key that starts a longer sequence, such as g. Alt+? opens it at any time.
- A help page opens once after you install DesertBird. It lists every key and command, and DesertBird builds it from your keymap, so it is always current. Press g? or ,h to open it again.
- Every command is defined once. Keys, the command line, completion and help all read the same definition.

It tells you what went wrong
A typo in a key, a command or a setting is an error with a message, never a silent no-op. The options page blocks a save that would break a binding.

What it covers
- Thread list: move, select, visual mode, archive, delete, move to a folder, mark, star, tag, undo.
- Reading: scroll, step through unread, open links with hints, find in a message.
- Compose: insert and normal mode, a mode label in the status bar, the keys of the address fields and an optional external editor.
- Quick filter keys, follow-up reminders and snooze.
- Tabs, panes, zoom and the context menu, all by key.
- Options page with a key editor and 16 built-in themes. One setting switches the theme for the popup, the command line and the mode label.
- Works in Thunderbird 153 ESR or later and in Betterbird.

Safe by design
DesertBird never runs the keys, commands or settings you type as code. It does not hold the permission to send mail. The one send key, gS in the compose window, does nothing until you turn on the compose_send setting, and then it runs Thunderbird's own send command with its checks. The bridge never sends mail. The part of the add-on that runs with extra privileges (an Experiment, which is how Thunderbird add-ons reach the parts of the program that the standard API does not cover) takes a fixed list of requests and has no way to run a script or open an address you type. Thunderbird shows a warning about full access to Thunderbird on install because of it. Its source is open and unminified.

Optional native host (Linux)
You do not need it. A small helper program, shared with the DesertFox Firefox add-on, adds two things: editing a message in your own editor (press Ctrl+E in the compose body) and a bridge that lets a desktop bar or a script talk to Thunderbird. You download and install it yourself. Thunderbird asks for the nativeMessaging permission only when you turn on the editor or the bridge setting and press Save. The bridge is off by default, and nothing connects while it is off. The helper takes a fixed set of requests and has no shell.

Privacy
DesertBird has no account, no telemetry, no analytics and makes no network requests of its own. Settings and state stay in Thunderbird storage on your device. The privacy policy lists what the optional bridge can pass to programs on your own computer when you turn its share settings on.

Source code, key list, issues and docs: https://github.com/uhs-robert/desertbird

version.approval_notes:
Build: BUILD.md at the root of the source archive. Node 24, npm ci, npm run build. The output is dist/ and the package is dist/desertbird.xpi. esbuild bundles our TypeScript and does not minify. The package holds nothing that is not built from src/ or vendor/ in the archive.

Vendored files: vendor/marked/marked.umd.js (marked 18.2.1, minified by its authors) and vendor/turndown/turndown.js (turndown 7.2.5) are the unchanged files of the npm release. The manifest loads them beside background.js and the build never bundles them. marked: https://registry.npmjs.org/marked/-/marked-18.2.1.tgz, npm integrity sha512-ii4bxCTCqqwpT86XZWgJNs+ZnAIZksmLGYMViWA7PDIXYIeNo1x6cDdX3JOip9NM/cI6p8z57FxliACboTruMA== . File package/lib/marked.umd.js has sha256 bb95d4c15f1289f78486eaacebf3bb18688475ed58a040ef762ed49337090542. turndown: https://registry.npmjs.org/turndown/-/turndown-7.2.5.tgz, npm integrity sha512-EKZvCCFHh8sWttpAMs10U6niZFJ2cpz8LkCPlylxoG4JcHF50J7EHnnBW3AY1qXtUMu7kDjCp7dnggB1sIbqEQ== . File package/dist/turndown.js has sha256 f46330e27d6009ecc3b001237e735cf58293772d2a465436a61de6f536b59a81. Both are MIT, with their LICENSE files in vendor/. vendor/desertfox/ is a pinned copy of MPL-2.0 source of our own sibling project (see its VENDOR.md) and compiles into background.js.

Remote code: none. The add-on makes no network request of its own and has no host it contacts. Every script and page is in the package. It never evaluates a string: keys, commands and settings pass through one validator against a fixed command registry.

Why an Experiment: the MailExtension API gives no key handling in the mail window, no thread list cursor or focus, no folder pane control, no compose window key runtime and no control of open native menus. docs/thunderbird-behavior.md holds the measurements behind each choice and docs/design.md has a table of what the standard API covers and what needs the Experiment. There are eleven Experiment APIs, all with scope addon_parent only: keys, app, folderpane, overlay, menukeys, composewin, pages, zoom, context, hints and filter. Four ES module files (experiment/*.sys.mjs) run as window actors. The Experiment files are unminified so they can be read as shipped. Each has a size guard in tools/build.mjs.

The Experiment takes a fixed table of verbs. Every verb has typed args that its schema checks (experiment/*.schema.json). No verb takes a free string to run, a script or a URL. app.command takes a name from a fixed allowlist of Thunderbird commands, and app.open_page takes a key of a fixed table of internal pages, never an address. test/design_verbs.test.ts fails when a verb of a schema is missing from the list in docs/design.md.

TODO-CHROME-VERBS: the owner fills this section with the final list of chrome verbs, including folderpane.viewFindRow. Do not submit while this line is present. The list in docs/design.md, section "Chrome verbs", is the source.

Page actor (experiment/page_actor_child.sys.mjs and page_actor_parent.sys.mjs): it gives keys to web pages, file:// pages and the pages of other add-ons in a tab of a main window, so the user can scroll and use hints on them. It keeps this full reach on purpose, and these protections limit it. (1) It attaches only to pages in a tab of a main window. The add-on's own pages, message documents, compose and about: pages are not matched, and a frame inside a page is not matched either. (2) The child reads a key and one bit, whether the focus is in a text field. It sends only keys that the parent's key table lists (navigation keys and the keys that enter or leave insert mode) and never the text typed into a field. (3) The child takes no message that names code. The parent sends it only state (booleans and token lists), a scroll id from a fixed table with a count, a blur, or a hint pick with two colors and an action from a fixed set. (4) The parent rebuilds every message from the child field by field before the key runtime sees it, so a compromised page process cannot pass an unexpected field or command. (5) A child that has not been answered by the parent takes no key. The hint code loads on the first hint pick only.

Known low item: the chrome side decides that a message body owns its keys by the presence of the attribute data-desertbird-keys on the document root, and mail markup can carry that attribute. The effect is that DesertBird stops swallowing plain keys for a forged message frame, so Thunderbird's own single-key shortcuts act instead. It gives mail no way to run a command, so we judge it low and leave it for a later release, since a real fix needs a token that the parent checks.

Native host: not in the package. It is the optional Linux host of our DesertFox project, a separate download that the user installs by hand. nativeMessaging is an optional permission. The options page asks for it when the user turns on external_editor or bridge and presses Save. No native call is made without the grant, and the bridge setting is off by default. The host has a fixed set of verbs and no shell or eval verb. The commands that the bridge may run, and the never-list that wins over them, are in src/background/bridge/README.md and test/registry.test.ts.

Permissions:
- accountsFolders, accountsRead: folder commands, command line completion over folders and accounts, move, copy and go to a folder, create the Snoozed folder.
- messagesRead, messagesUpdate, messagesTags, messagesTagsList: read messages, set read state, star, junk and tags, and list tags for completion.
- messagesMove: archive, move, copy and trash.
- messagesDelete: the delete command. It moves a message to the Trash. In the Trash, the same command (two keys, dd) deletes for good.
- messagesModify: the message display script, which gives keys to a message document and hints on its links.
- compose, compose.save: reply, forward and new message, keys of the compose window, quick replies and drafts for the optional bridge. The add-on does not hold compose.send. The key gS (setting compose_send, off by default) runs Thunderbird's own send command in the compose window, with Thunderbird's checks, through a fixed chrome leaf. The bridge never sends.
- alarms: reminders and snooze.
- notifications: toasts for results, reminders and the optional new mail notice.
- storage: settings, keymap, marks, undo log, reminders and snoozes.
- tabs: tab commands.
- clipboardWrite: yank commands.
- downloads: the save attachments command (Downloads/DesertBird).
- optional nativeMessaging: the native host above.

Data collection: required is none. The add-on collects and transmits nothing. The optional bridge talks only to a local socket of programs on the user's own computer. docs/privacy.md is the privacy policy.
